candidates.name: case-domain-integrity
candidates.description: Pure domain schemas, graph invariants, normalized tags, deterministic search and filter selectors, readiness and lifecycle derivation, and transactional IndexedDB repository rules for a single-case evidence board.
candidates.reason: The same correctness rules repeat across local data, connections, closure, recall, search, capture, and backup: UUID and ISO validation, unordered pair keys, provenance eligibility, tag normalization, AND/OR filter semantics, cascade plans, derived readiness, and one transaction per mutation. No existing package covers this project-specific graph, query, and storage contract.

candidates.name: atomic-media-storage
candidates.description: Validated image ingestion, EXIF-aware derivative generation, attachment replacement, and failure-safe multi-table Blob transactions in local IndexedDB.
candidates.reason: Evidence Capture, OCR, and Backup all depend on atomic card and attachment writes, replacement-before-delete ordering, object URL cleanup, and zero orphan Blobs. This is a fragile repeated process with no suitable existing package.

candidates.name: pixi-case-board
candidates.description: PixiJS 8 case-board rendering, viewport math, card gestures, culling, texture release, string geometry, recall scratch rendering, and teardown for a 150-card tablet target.
candidates.reason: Project rules such as 0.25 to 2.5 zoom, 500 ms touch lift, 6 px tap tolerance, 12 px string sag, 200 resident textures, 150-card culling, recall scratch mode, and complete teardown are not covered by the generic PixiJS API package.

candidates.name: pixijs
candidates.description: Upstream PixiJS v8 API guidance for Application setup, scene graph, events, assets, ticker, performance, and teardown.
candidates.reason: The global PixiJS skill package already satisfies the library API learning need. Do not vendor a local copy; the project-specific board behavior lives in pixi-case-board.

candidates.name: accessible-case-ui
candidates.description: React DOM patterns for the case-file UI: semantic dialogs and sheets, focus restoration, live announcements, 44 px targets, keyboard paths, and reduced motion.
candidates.reason: Accessibility is implemented per feature and audited later. Repeated focus-trap, restore, target, announcement, sheet, shortcut, and reduced-motion rules need a project-local checklist rather than a generic component guide.

candidates.name: local-first-backup-archive
candidates.description: Versioned .ndcase ZIP export and hardened import validation with checksums, path-safety, ID remapping, copy-versus-replace semantics, and rollback.
candidates.reason: Backup is the product's main data-loss mitigation and carries repeated security and transaction rules: traversal rejection, duplicate and oversized entries, checksums, manifest versions, ID remapping, replace confirmation, and failure rollback. No existing package covers this archive contract.

candidates.name: offline-pwa-release
candidates.description: Offline-first PWA release process for GitHub Pages: relative base paths, service-worker precache, same-origin asset audits, bundle budgets, and update prompts.
candidates.reason: GitHub Pages, hash routing, bundled OCR wasm and traineddata, no third-party requests, and the 300 KB initial and 25 MB precache budgets create a fragile release path repeated across foundation, release, and verification tasks.

candidates.name: browser-evidence-journeys
candidates.description: Playwright browser evidence for real IndexedDB, file input, downloads, offline reload, viewport matrices, axe scans, and performance floors.
candidates.reason: The PRD rejects mock-only or build-only evidence. Repeated journeys must exercise real persistence, native file input, real archives, offline contexts, viewport-specific overflow, axe scans, and measured frame performance.

candidates.name: ocr-worker-lifecycle
candidates.description: Bundled tesseract.js worker lifecycle with same-origin assets, a single job at a time, timeout and cancel cleanup, and non-destructive title suggestions.
candidates.reason: OCR is optional but fragile: worker, wasm, and English traineddata must be copied, precached, and resolved same-origin; only one job may run; cancel and timeout must terminate cleanly; and OCR must never overwrite an edited title. No existing package covers this lifecycle.

candidates.name: demo-case-seeding
candidates.description: Locally generated, clearly marked demo case fixture and one-time seed and removal behavior that is isolated from user cases.
candidates.reason: The demo is a single, mostly one-off content fixture. The domain, media, and transactional seeding guidance already covers the implementation, so a dedicated package is not justified.

candidates.name: human-acceptance-review
candidates.description: Structured human review gates for visual direction, board feel, accessibility spot checks, and final field acceptance.
candidates.reason: These gates must be executed by a person and cannot be encoded as agent instructions. The review JSON files and checklists already live in the feature tasks and orchestrator gates.

candidates.name: tdd
candidates.description: Test-first red-green-refactor workflow for unit, component, and integration work.
candidates.reason: A generic TDD package already satisfies the workflow need. Project-specific evidence requirements are covered by browser-evidence-journeys and the feature acceptance criteria.
